name: The Langham Boston
positioning: Historic former Federal Reserve Bank building turned hotel in Boston's Financial District, officially called The Langham, Boston
best_for: Travelers who like staying in a historic building with local art
Families wanting suites and a Club lounge

facts.text: The building is a protected historic landmark under the Boston Landmarks Commission.
The hotel's art collection pays homage to the building's banking history and local heritage.
The Fed is a street-level bar serving pub fare, raw-bar seafood and cocktails.
The Langham Club offers full breakfast with an omelet station, afternoon snacks, and evening cocktails and a light dinner.
The hotel has a bilevel 24-hour fitness center, a heated indoor pool, a hot tub and saunas.
Every subway line intersects near the hotel, giving easy access to outer neighborhoods.
The minibars are stocked with Massachusetts-sourced goods.
The Chairman Suite has a walk-in closet, a fireplace and a piano.
The hotel sources most of its ingredients from New England purveyors and businesses.
The hotel is ADA-compliant with wheelchair-accessible rooms and elevators.

highlights.text: The building dates from 1922 and was formerly the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston before being converted into a hotel in 1981.
The former bank left behind two early-20th-century N.C. Wyeth murals.
Grana, the hotel's Italian restaurant, sits in a former bank hall with French chandeliers, original stone floors and a three-dimensional Lady Liberty head.
Guests of Club Rooms and Suites have complimentary access to The Langham Club.
The Club Bi-Level Family Suite spans two floors with a living area, pull-out sofa and half bath downstairs and the master bedroom upstairs.

considerations.text: The hotel has no spa; it offers a fitness center, heated indoor pool, hot tub and saunas instead.
Access to The Langham Club is included with Club Rooms and Suites.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: The Langham, Boston
